The purpose of this paper is to report and discuss the results of an atom probe' analysis on some single crystal superalloys in order to clarify the role of Re, on an ato- mic scale, in improving the creep strength.
Single crystals were grown parallel to the [001] orientation using the seeded technique under a temperature gradient of 250°C/cm and at a withdrawal rate of 15 cm/hour.
All specimens were given a solutionlng and homogenizing treatment between 1280 and 1325°C for 15 hours followed by air quenching
the following precipitation heat treatment : IIO0°C/4h/AC + 850°C/48h/

By comparing the two distributions with the help of a statistical ~2 test, it can be concluded that a significant number of small Re-enrlched regions is present. Short range order therefore occurs for Re in the matrix of these alloys.
The rhenium profile clearly exhibits a small enriched region extending over 1.3 nm.
Atom-probe microanalyses of various Re containing alloys clearly revealed the occurence of short range order in the matrix.

The Re clusters can act as more efficient obstacles against dislocation motion compared to the isolated solute atoms in a solid solution. It is thought that these clusters play a significant role in improving the creep strength of Re-containing superalloys.
